title: Jenkins
novel:
Marshall worked at a law firm with a man named Jenkins. Jenkins was [[reckless|reckless]], loud, and fond of a drinking game he had invented — one that left everyone [[humiliated|humiliate]] by morning.

Robin, meanwhile, had a new co-host named Don. He was [[sloppy|sloppy]], rude, and seemed to [[deliberately|deliberately]] ruin every broadcast. Robin [[despised|despise]] him.

Lily grew [[jealous|jealous]] when Marshall mentioned a female coworker. She [[suspected|suspect]] an affair, though Marshall only talked about Jenkins.

One night Jenkins kissed Marshall at a bar — a [[prank|prank]] meant to [[embarrass|embarrass]] him. Marshall [[panicked|panic]]. He did not know how to tell Lily.

When he finally [[confessed|confess]], Lily only laughed. "I was never jealous of Jenkins," she said. "I was jealous of your job taking you from me."

Robin's show [[debuted|debut]] that week to terrible reviews, mostly because of Don. Some [[rivalries|rivalry]], Ted observed, were the start of something neither side expected.

reckless.en: doing things without thinking of danger

humiliate.en: to make someone feel ashamed in public

despise.en: to hate someone or something very much

jealous.en: angry that someone you like is with another

suspect.en: to think that something is true, without being sure

prank.en: a trick played on someone for fun

embarrass.en: to make someone feel shy or ashamed

panic.en: to feel sudden fear and not know what to do

confess.en: to admit something you tried to hide

debut.en: to appear in public for the first time

rivalry.en: a continuing competition between two sides
